issues.issue: After enumerating specific classes the definition sweeps in 'in general, any Certificates that do not satisfy the applicable ratings requirement under the Underwriter's Exemption,' a catch-all with no stated boundary against the listed specifics. Whether a class outside the enumeration can be ERISA-Restricted depends on how that residual phrase is read.

The definition is textually truncated — it opens mid-phrase with a stray filing URL and the word 'Certificates' rather than a complete definitional sentence. What term is being defined and its full content cannot be read off the provision itself.

This sentence nullifies unidentified 'defined terms and provisions herein' relating to rating agencies other than Moody's, S&P and Fitch, so its effect can only be determined by running it against every rating-agency reference in the Agreement (for example the rating conditions in Section 11.01 amendments). Which provisions it strikes is not visible from its own words.

Accrual Period is defined only for the Delay Certificates and the No Delay Certificates, but the Preliminary Statement provides that the Class C Certificates accrue interest at a variable Pass-Through Rate and the Class C Certificates fall in neither category. The accrual convention for those classes must be supplied from elsewhere in the instrument.

The definition caps rates at the Pass-Through Rate 'determined without regard to the Available Funds Rate Cap,' but the Preliminary Statement fixes each Pass-Through Rate by reference to the Net Rate Cap, of which the Available Funds Rate Cap is only one input. Reading the two together it is unclear what rate is to be used.

The definition turns on whether a Person 'directly or indirectly controls or is controlled by or is under common control with' another, but 'control' is nowhere defined or given a threshold. The scope of Affiliate is therefore open at its edges.

The phrase 'at the close of business on the related Servicer Remittance Date' is repeated twice in the same sentence, once before and once after the reference to the Mortgage Loan. The duplication garbles what is being measured at that date.

The definition excepts only the Interest Only Certificates from 'the aggregate Class Principal Balance of all Classes of Certificates,' leaving it unclear whether the Class C and Class P Certificates are counted in the comparison. Whether they are counted changes the size of the Applied Realized Loss Amount.

For a Refinancing Mortgage Loan the value is 'the appraisal made at the time of the origination ... as modified by an updated appraisal,' without saying when, by whom or on what standard an updated appraisal is made or whether one is required. The trailing qualifier leaves the value indeterminate.

The definition cross-refers to 'Section 3.22(i)(a),' a subsection designation that does not match the lettering scheme used elsewhere for Section 3.22 (e.g., Section 3.22(b)(i) for the Accountant's Attestation). The referent of the definition must be reconstructed.

The Certificate Insurer becomes Auction Initiator only if the Class C Certificateholder 'has not exercised its rights ... on any date on which [it] is entitled to do so,' but no cut-off date or notice mechanic fixes when that condition is satisfied. Because the right is a continuing one, when it passes to the Certificate Insurer is indeterminate.

The lettering repeats: clause (b) is itself defined as 'the excess, if any, of (a) the Principal Funds ... over (b) the Overcollateralization Release Amount,' reusing (a) and (b) inside limb (b). The nesting error makes the arithmetic of the definition ambiguous on its face.

The list 'banking institutions in the City of New York, New York, Minnesota, Maryland' mixes a city with bare state names and no city, so it is unclear whether closure anywhere in Minnesota or Maryland suffices. The mechanical defect changes which days are Business Days.

The Cap Account is said to be established 'pursuant to 3.07(i) of this agreement,' a citation lacking the word Section and not matching the subsection lettering used for the parallel Carryover Reserve Fund (Section 3.07(h)). The governing subsection has to be located by inference.

This definition has the Certificates executed and authenticated by the Trust Administrator, while Section 11.10 speaks of the Certificates 'upon due authentication thereof by the Trustee pursuant to this Agreement.' Which officer's authentication validates a Certificate cannot be settled from either provision alone.
